To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the microstructure of sodium-activated calcium bentoneite in wet iron ore green pellet is a voluminous, dispersed, and interconnected network, and in the dry pellet, bentonite forms solid bridges that impart strength to the compact.
bentonite in iron ore green pellets is a voluminous network of clay tactoids in wet pellets, and in dry pellets, it is a network of clay tactoid bridges between mineral particles.

the microstructure of sodium-activated calcium bentoneite is revealed in iron ore green pellets using scanning electron microscopy, cryogenic methods (high pressure freezing and plunge freezng in liquid ethane), low loss backscaterring electrons, monochromatic imaging at low voltage, and decelerated electron beam imaging.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the microstructure of sodium-activated calcium bentoneite in wet and dried iron ore green pellets as well as in water.
the effect of the microstructure of the bentonite in iron ore green pellets on pellet strength and pellet quality.
the understanding the role of clay in wet and dry green pellets.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the microstructure of sodium bentonite in iron ore green pellets is a result of the interplay of the following three factors: the type of iron ore (magnetite), the type of bentonite (sodium bentonite) and the processing steps (wetting and drying).
bentonite is a binder in iron-ore green pellets.
bentonite microstructure in wet iron ore green magnetite pellets is different from the microstructure of the same bentonite in dry pellets and in distilled water.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the microstructure of the clay in the wet iron ore green pellet is different from that of the clay in a dry iron ore pellet.
the microstructure of the iron ore pellets is very much dependent on the water content of the pellet.

bentonite is a highly plastic clay, which is capable of forming voluminous networks of tactoids, and the tactoids are drawn into the interstices between mineral particles and form bridges when the pellet is dried, which is the reason for the strength of bentonite bonded iron ore pellets.
The main takeaway from our work is that
bentonite in the iron ore green pellets forms a three-dimensional network of clay platelets in the wet state.
, contrary to what has been reported in the past, bentonite is present in iron ore pellets as clay tactoids (i.e., stacks of parallel primary clay particles) rather than as individual platelets.
bentonite in iron ore green pellets is very well hydrated, and this is the main cause of the strength increase of the green pellet.
